<head>
    <meta charset="utf-8" />
    <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1" />
    <meta name="theme-color" content="#1f6b4a" />
    <title>Washington heat pump rebate calculator (2026) · Sourced Calc</title>
    <meta
      name="description"
      content="Conservative 2026 Washington heat pump rebate estimate from public PSE, Seattle Clean Heat, City Light, Commerce HEAR, and IRS pages. Not a quote."
    />
    <link rel="canonical" href="https://sourcedcalc.com/wa-heat-pump-rebate/" />
    <link rel="icon" href="../favicon.ico" sizes="any" />
    <link rel="icon" href="../favicon.svg" type="image/svg+xml" />

    <script async src="https://www.googletagmanager.com/gtag/js?id=G-3SB1LCNKZK"></script>
    <script src="../ga.js"></script>
    <script type="application/ld+json">
      {
        "@context": "https://schema.org",
        "@type": "FAQPage",
        "mainEntity": [
          {
            "@type": "Question",
            "name": "Can I budget an $8,000 federal HARP rebate for a Washington heat pump in 2026?",
            "acceptedAnswer": {
              "@type": "Answer",
              "text": "No. Washington’s federal HARP and HOMES programs are not live. Commerce is evaluating U.S. Department of Energy program notices dated June 1, 2026. Do not budget $8,000 or any HARP/HOMES amount for a 2026 install. Federal 25C and 25D tax credits also ended December 31, 2025 for property placed in service / expenditures after that date."
            }
          },
          {
            "@type": "Question",
            "name": "What is the PSE heat pump rebate in 2026?",
            "acceptedAnswer": {
              "@type": "Answer",
              "text": "Published PSE figures: $1,500 standard or $2,400 Efficiency Boost (PSE’s own income table; Trade Ally or REP) for electric resistance → air-source heat pump, and the same $1,500 / $2,400 Boost for heat-pump-to-heat-pump when the existing unit is a centrally ducted all-electric heat pump out of original manufacturer warranty (Trade Ally). Income-qualified full gas switch: $4,000 on PSE’s table — not automatic 150% AMI. Hybrid gas furnace path: the flyer lists $1,500 / $2,400 Boost; older PDFs conflict — treat as verify. Do not add hybrid + $4,000. No published oil-to-heat-pump rebate; oil furnaces, boilers, and wall heaters are not eligible for the electric-resistance $1,500 / $2,400 conversion."
            }
          },
          {
            "@type": "Question",
            "name": "What is Seattle’s oil Clean Heat rebate?",
            "acceptedAnswer": {
              "@type": "Answer",
              "text": "Seattle Clean Heat (oil → qualifying Mitsubishi, participating contractor): $2,000 instant at any income, plus an extra $4,000 bonus for 81%–150% AMI if installed by September 30, 2026 (up to $6,000). Lower-income households may have a free Office of Housing conversion — do not treat Housing marketing averages as a rebate dollar. Seattle City Light also lists contractor instant discounts under 5.4 tons: $300 (SEER2 15.2 / HSPF2 ≥ 8.1), $400 (SEER2 15.2 / HSPF2 ≥ 8.5), $600 (SEER2 16.0 / HSPF2 ≥ 9.5). DIY is not eligible. Stacking Clean Heat + the City Light discount is not confirmed additive — verify."
            }
          },
          {
            "@type": "Question",
            "name": "Who qualifies for Washington HEAR?",
            "acceptedAnswer": {
              "@type": "Answer",
              "text": "State HEAR is for households at or under 150% AMI using HUD county income limits (plus some small businesses and adult family homes). Commerce does not publish a statewide heat-pump dollar. Local third-party administrators set amounts. Email HomeRebates@Commerce.wa.gov and put “State Home Electrification and Appliance Rebates (HEAR) Program” in the subject line."
            }
          }
        ]
      }
    </script>
  </head>
